title: Lonepine Commerce - Onramp Handoff & Implementation Kickoff
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-04-08
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Location: Zoom
Links shared: onboarding_playbook_v1.pdf, network_diagram.png, sla-pricing-sheet.xlsx

Summary:
Quick intro, scope alignment, network and security prerequisites, plan for a 6-week pilot (staging -> canary -> prod), next steps to schedule a network workshop and provide Dedicated capacity quote.

Topics:
- Pilot scope and success metrics
- Connectivity (VPC peering, IP allowlists)
- Data residency and KMS
- Rollout plan and SLAs
- Resource/ops contacts and runbook ownership

Transcript:
[00:00] Ava (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. I'm Ava, AE for Lonepine, and with me is Diego from the solutions team and Janelle our CSM. How's everyone doing?
[00:12] Meera (CTO): Good, thanks. Excited to get this kicked off. We had our execs greenlit a pilot so today is really about lining up next steps.
[00:22] Diego (Redwood SE): Nice. We'll run through the proposed sprint plan and then dig into network and security. Quick note — apologies in advance if audio drops, I'm on slightly spotty wifi.
[00:32] Samir (Head of ML): No problem. We'll record and follow up. Our immediate goal is an inference pilot for chat and embeddings behind our web app, low-latency for search ranking.
[00:42] Janelle (CSM): Great. I put a rough 6-week timeline in the deck — week 0 network/workshop, week 1-3 staging pilot, week 4 canary in prod, week 5-6 optimization and handover.
[00:55] Priya (DevOps): Two quick constraints: we need VPC-only connectivity, and our security team insists on KMS integration + audit logs retained for 1 year.
[01:06] Ethan (Security): Also SOC2 attestation is required; we'll need the security pack and SOC2 report before prod rollout.
[01:14] Ava: Absolutely — we can share our security pack today, and I'll add SOC2 + penetration testing artifacts. Diego, can you summarize the VPC options available?
[01:24] Diego: Sure. There are three: hosted API over TLS with private link (managed), Redwood Dedicated in your VPC (customer-managed nodes), or Private deployment (on-prem or air-gapped). For most customers needing VPC peering we do Dedicated with a control-plane handshake. Dedicated gives predictable throughput and you can bring your KMS.
[01:42] Lucas (Product): Cost will matter. If Dedicated is expensive for the pilot, can we start hosted and migrate?
[01:48] Diego: You can. There are tradeoffs — hosted is faster to start but doesn't meet strict VPC-only or KMS requirements. We can do hybrid: start with hosted for feature validation, then move pilot traffic to Dedicated. But that adds migration engineering time.
[02:03] Meera: Success metrics — below 120ms p95 for short prompts and embedding latency < 200ms for the search path. Also cost per 1M tokens under $X (we set a target internally).
[02:16] Janelle: Noted. We'll bake those into the pilot SLA. Diego, do we have benchmark tooling?
[02:21] Diego: Yes — we'll run a small load harness and share a spreadsheet with latency percentiles and token cost estimates. Expect a preliminary benchmark in 7 days after staging is up.
[02:33] Priya: For networking, our infra team requires an IP allowlist and mutual TLS for the control channel. Is that supported?
[02:40] Diego: IP allowlists and mTLS are supported on Dedicated and Private. For hosted we can do private link + allowlist but not mTLS to the control plane. We'll detail that in the network diagram I shared.
[02:55] Ethan: Regarding logs — we need audit logs pushed to our Splunk instance and access via role-based access control (RBAC).
[03:03] Diego: We can forward audit logs to your syslog/Splunk via a secure forwarder. RBAC and SSO using your SAML IdP are supported for the console.
[03:12] Meera: Who will own the runbook for fallbacks? If the model degrades we need automatic fallback to a cheaper variant and circuit breaker alerts.
[03:22] Ava: We recommend a canary plus automatic fallback policy. Diego, we have a template runbook in the onboarding playbook — point them to the resend.
[03:31] Diego: Will do. Template includes thresholds and escalation paths.
[03:36] Lucas: On roles — who's our day-to-day contact for troubleshooting?
[03:40] Janelle: I'll be the CSM and primary operational contact; Diego is the SE for technical escalations; Ava will handle commercial.
[03:46] Samir: A short technical question — we use KV cache aggressively in our app, how does Redwood handle cache warming and key persistence during failover?
[03:55] Diego: Redwood's runtime supports KV cache snapshotting to speed warmup during node restart; on Dedicated you can persist cache snapshots to ephemeral storage shared across the pool. We'll detail the behavior and warmup times in the tech appendix.
[04:12] Priya: Any recommended quantization or model variant for lower cost?
[04:17] Diego: For production search/load we typically start with an FP16 variant then evaluate int8 quantized models for cost savings. Redwood Optimize will give model/quantization recs based on your workload.
[04:27] Meera: Ok. Timeline question — if we decide Dedicated, how long to provision?
[04:32] Ava: Provisioning Dedicated capacity typically takes 2-3 weeks depending on region and commit; we can accelerate for pilots with short-term burst capacity.
[04:40] Ethan: Pen testing — do you allow customer-initiated scans on staging? We need to run our SAST/DAST against it.
[04:47] Diego: Yes, with notice and within the agreed window. We'll include scan parameters in the security pack.
[04:55] Janelle: I'll send the security pack and SOC2 today, and we can set up a network workshop with your infra team.
[05:03] Meera: Good. On success criteria, we also need clear rollback windows and a plan if latency regresses after rollout.
[05:10] Diego: We'll include rollback playbooks and a canary percentage ramp schedule in the runbook.
[05:17] Samir: A small ask — can we get a sample prompt set and eval suite run against the pilot model before canary?
[05:24] Janelle: Yes, please upload that to the shared drive. We'll tie quality regression alerts to that eval set.
[05:31] Priya: Network workshop availability — our infra people are available next Wednesday and Friday.
[05:36] Ava: We'll aim for Wednesday 10am your time.
[05:40] Lucas: Contract question — do we sign a short pilot MSA or just an addendum?
[05:45] Ava: Typically a pilot addendum to our MSA is fine; I'll coordinate with legal.
[05:50] Ethan: One last security ask — KMS key rotation policy alignment; we need keys rotated every 90 days and evidence of key access audits.
[05:59] Diego: We support customer-managed keys and can align rotation policies; audit logs for key usage will be included.
[06:08] Meera: Great. Anything else from Redwood?
[06:11] Ava: We'll send the Dedicated capacity quote and pilot pricing, security pack, and a proposed 6-week plan. Also propose a staging access checklist.
[06:20] Samir: Sounds good. We'll prepare the prompt set and security questionnaire.
[06:24] Janelle: I'll create the shared Slack channel and add runbook docs.
[06:27] Priya: Thanks.
[06:30] Ava: Ok quick recap and next steps then close.

Action items mentioned in call (in transcript):
- Ava to send Dedicated capacity quote and pricing spreadsheet.
- Janelle to share security pack and SOC2 artifacts.
- Diego to schedule network workshop and attach network diagram details.
- Samir/Priya to upload prompt set and security questionnaire to shared drive.

(Transcript ends — recording stopped at 16:48 UTC)
